Choose which name components are hidden per actor in Randomizer → Name, or set a per-token override in the token's configuration. Note: this hides the name in the interface only; a determined player can still read the real name via the browser console.

TR.Tab.Name: Name
TR.Ability.EnableHint: When enabled, ability scores will be randomized when an unlinked token of this actor is placed on a scene.
TR.Ability.ConstraintsHint: Set minimum and maximum values for each ability score. Scores will be assigned and clamped to fit these ranges.
TR.Ability.PriorityHint: When enabled, abilities with higher priority (6 = highest) will receive higher scores. Equal priorities are assigned randomly. Priority is secondary to min/max constraints.
TR.Ability.NilHint: Check Nil to leave an ability blank ("—") instead of assigning a score — the modifier becomes +0 and the ability is treated as absent (e.g. mindless creatures with no Intelligence). This is not the same as a score of 0, which gives a −5 modifier.
TR.Name.EnableHint: When enabled, the token name is assembled from the components below when an unlinked token is placed.
TR.Name.BuilderHint: The name is built by joining each component, left to right, with spaces. Components resolving to nothing are skipped.
TR.Name.NoComponents: No components yet — add one below to start building the name.
TR.Name.DbInfo: {count} names loaded ({given} given, {surname} surname). Manage the name database and adjective lists in Game Settings → Token Randomizer Lists.
TR.Adj.NoLists: No adjective lists are defined. Add lists from Game Settings → Token Randomizer Lists.
TR.Adj.Hint: Check the lists to draw from and set each one's weight. A list is picked by weight, then a random word from it.
TR.Obscure.Label: Visibility
TR.Obscure.Hint: Real name only hides this component from non-observers; Obscured name only shows it only to them (a decoy).
TR.Obscure.AltHint: Optional. Non-observers see this text in place of the component. Leave blank to simply drop the component for them.
TR.TokenConfig.ObscureHint: When on, users without Observer permission on this token see the obscured name below instead of its real name.
TR.TokenConfig.ObscuredNameHint: Shown to non-observers. Auto-filled from the Name tab when a token is placed; edit here to override it for this token.
TR.Treasure.EnableHint: When enabled, the actor's carried currency (pp/gp/sp/cp) is generated and replaced when an unlinked token of this actor is placed on a scene.
TR.Treasure.TotalValueHint: Total treasure value in gold pieces. Supports dice and actor data, e.g. 2d6*100 or @cr * 50 (@cr = the actor's total CR).
TR.Treasure.CoinDistributionHint: Share of the total value held in each coin type (computed as gold-equivalent, then converted to coins). Each coin count is rounded down.
TR.Treasure.RandomizeHintOn: A random weight is picked within each coin's Min/Max (0–100), then the four weights are normalized into proportions of the total value.
TR.Treasure.RandomizeHintOff: The four percentages are normalized by their sum, so they need not add up to exactly 100.
TR.Lists.NameDbInfo: {count} names loaded ({given} given, {surname} surname). Your custom database is stored in the world folder and replaces the bundled sample once you import.
TR.Lists.ImportHint: Import CSV / TSV / TXT (header row with a name column; optional type (given/surname), race, region, gender) or JSON ({ "names": [...] }). A missing type is treated as given. Imports merge; exact duplicates are skipped.
TR.Lists.AdjHint: Single-column word lists used by Adjective name segments. Bundled lists ship with the module; uploading a list with the same name overrides it, and any other name adds a new list. Upload a TXT (one word per line), CSV, or JSON array.
TR.StatMethods.Title: Custom Stat Methods
TR.StatMethods.Intro: Define reusable generation methods that appear in the Ability Scores method dropdown, alongside the built-in arrays and random methods. There are two kinds:
TR.StatMethods.ArrayHelp: Array — six fixed values, like Standard/Elite/Champion. Order does not matter; the values are assigned to abilities using each actor's min/max and priority settings.
TR.StatMethods.FormulaHelp: Formula — a dice formula rolled once per ability. Uses the same syntax as other formula fields, e.g. 4d6dl1 (4d6, drop lowest), 3d6, or 2d6+6.
TR.StatMethods.NoMethods: No custom methods yet. Add an array or a formula below.
TR.Skill.EnableHint: Deals skill ranks when an unlinked token is placed.
TR.Skill.BudgetDeferred: Budget is calculated per actor at placement.
TR.Skill.BudgetZeroHint: No class items, so no ranks are owed. Add a class (racial HD count).
TR.Skill.NoClassSkills: This actor has no class skills.
TR.Skill.ListHint: Weight 1–10, relative to each other. A row covering several skills (Knowledge, Craft) counts as one.
TR.Skill.NoEntries: None. Every skill still gets ranks by group weight.
TR.Skill.SubSkillRequired: Add an entry or group — this skill holds no ranks itself.
TR.Skill.GroupTitle: Group — one member is drawn at random for each token
TR.Skill.ExcludedHint: Never touched: no ranks, and never cleared. Points with nowhere else to go are lost.
TR.Skill.WipeExistingHint: Off = add on top of the ranks the actor already has. On = zero every skill first, so the result is this roll alone. Excluded skills are never cleared.
TR.SkillProfile.Title: Skill Profiles
TR.SkillProfile.Intro: Saved skill-randomizer settings that can be loaded onto any actor from the Skills tab. Rename, reorder or delete them here. To change what a profile contains, load it in the defaults dialog, edit it, and save it again under the same name.
TR.SkillProfile.NoProfiles: No profiles saved yet. Create one from the Skills tab of any actor's randomizer dialog, or from Configure Defaults.

TR.SubSkillGroup.Title: Subskill Groups
TR.SubSkillGroup.Intro: A group is a named set of specialities under one skill — for example Smithing under Craft, holding Weaponsmithing, Armorsmithing and Blacksmithing. Use a group in the Skills tab and each token draws one of its members at random. Only Craft, Perform, Profession, Art and Lore have specialities, so only they can host a group.

TR.Notif.SubSkillGroupDuplicate: More than one {skill} group is named "{name}". Names must be unique within a skill.
TR.Skill.ProfileLoadTitle: Replace these settings with the selected profile
TR.Skill.ProfileSaveTitle: Save these settings as a reusable profile
TR.Skill.BackgroundHint: Background ranks only go to background skills. Leftovers are lost.
TR.Skill.GroupsHint:
Weight — odds of a rank going to that group. 0 = only if nothing else has room. Within the skill list, entry weights decide which one; class and other skills are picked evenly.
Focus — chance the next rank repeats the same skill. 10 = fill one skill before moving on.
TR.SubSkillGroup.KnownIntro: Suggestions offered when typing a speciality name in the Skills tab. Press Enter to add one. Typing something not listed is still allowed.
